newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian government seen winning confidence votes.
newsitem.headline: Belgian government seen winning confidence votes.

text.p: Belgium's four-party coalition government will face a series of confidence votes in parliament later on Thursday but is expected to win them all after its members patched up differences earlier in the week over a corruption scandal.

The motions of confidence were submitted by opposition parties last week after police arrested members of the French-speaking PS socialist party, the second largest in the coalition, in connection with allegations the party received bribes from French plane maker Dassault in the 1980s.

However, the strongest motions -- withdrawing confidence in the government -- have been submitted by opposition parties which represent only 16 members of the 150-seat assembly. Voting begins around four p.m. (1500 gmt).

A motion from the VLD and PRL liberal parties (the largest opposition grouping, with a combined 39 seats) would force the socialist ministers in the government to resign. The two parties last week offered to replace the socialists.
The coalition, which has 82 seats, will seek to push through a motion which, while condemning corruption, "invites the government to continue its programme and to face new social challenges."

The coalition looked set to split earlier this week when the chairman of the Flemish Christian Democratic party said it would be a "problem" if leading PS party figure Guy Spitaels, who has been implicated in the Dassault affair, continued to head the regional Walloon parliament.
Spitaels said on Wednesday, after his protective parliamentary immunity was removed by the assembly, that he would take a "holiday" while being questioned by police.
He said he had no knowledge of the alleged bribes being paid in the late 1980s, when he was chairman of the party, and was willing to help the judicial inquiry.
